title: Android Testing
description: Beginner-to-advanced Android testing reference for strategy, unit and instrumented tests, test doubles, coroutines and Flow, Compose UI, navigation, storage, reliability, and CI.

sections.title: Testing Strategy
sections.description: Build confidence around user-visible risks rather than maximizing raw test count.

subtopics.title: Unit, Integration, UI & End-to-End
subtopics.description: Use fast local tests for decision-heavy logic, integration tests for boundaries, UI tests for behavior and navigation, and a small number of critical end-to-end journeys.

table.title: Android Test Level Selection
rows: Repository with Room or network fake
Critical user journey across the app

codeBlocks.code:
Unit: pure functions, use cases, ViewModels, reducers
Integration: repository + fake server/database, serialization, migrations
UI/component: one screen, semantics, user actions, state rendering
Navigation: destination transitions and back behavior
End-to-end: a few release-critical journeys on realistic infrastructure

callouts.title: Test Observable Behavior
callouts.text: Assert outputs, state, persisted records, and visible semantics. Tests coupled to private methods or call order block safe refactoring without adding confidence.

subtopics.title: Risk-Based Coverage
subtopics.description: Prioritize money, identity, data loss, permissions, migrations, offline behavior, concurrency, process restoration, accessibility, and critical journeys.

codeBlocks.code:
For each feature test:
1. Happy path and user-visible result
2. Empty/loading/error/retry states
3. Boundary values and malformed external input
4. Cancellation, duplicate actions, and races
5. Rotation/process recreation where state matters
6. Accessibility semantics and large content
7. Persistence or network contract changes

callouts.title: Coverage Is a Clue
callouts.text: Line coverage can reveal untested code but cannot prove useful assertions, correct concurrency, or covered user journeys. Mutation testing and defect history provide stronger signals.

sections.title: Local JVM Unit Tests
sections.description: Keep most business logic free of Android runtime dependencies so tests remain fast and deterministic.

subtopics.title: Arrange, Act, Assert
subtopics.description: Name tests as behavior statements and keep one reason for failure per test.

callouts.title: One Concept, Useful Failure
callouts.text: Parameterized tests are excellent for input matrices; separate scenarios when a failure should explain different behavior or require different setup.

subtopics.title: ViewModel State Tests
subtopics.description: Construct the ViewModel with fakes, trigger public actions, and assert its public state contract.

callouts.title: Test the Contract
callouts.text: Avoid asserting that a particular private coroutine or helper was invoked. Assert the state, repository effect, or navigation decision consumers can observe.

sections.title: Fakes, Stubs, Spies & Mocks
sections.description: Choose the simplest controllable substitute that preserves useful behavior.

subtopics.title: Prefer Fakes for Stateful Boundaries
subtopics.description: Fakes implement a working simplified contract; stubs return configured answers; spies record calls; mocks define interaction expectations.

callouts.title: A Fake Is Shared Test Infrastructure
callouts.text: Keep fakes faithful to important contract semantics such as uniqueness, ordering, and errors. Overly permissive fakes let invalid production usage pass.

subtopics.title: When Interaction Verification Helps
subtopics.description: Verify calls when the call itself is the contract: analytics, notifications, external commands, or ensuring a dangerous action happens once.

callouts.title: Avoid Overspecification
callouts.text: Do not verify every collaborator call or exact ordering unless required by behavior. Such tests mirror implementation and become refactoring taxes.

sections.title: Coroutines, Flow & Virtual Time
sections.description: Use one scheduler and explicit collection so asynchronous tests remain deterministic.

subtopics.title: runTest & Test Dispatchers
subtopics.description: runTest supplies a TestScope and scheduler, skips virtual delays, propagates child failures, and waits for scheduled work.

codeBlocks.code:
@Test
fun `refresh waits then publishes content`() = runTest {
    val dispatcher = StandardTestDispatcher(testScheduler)
    val repository = FakeRepository(delayMs = 1_000)
    val vm = FeedViewModel(repository, dispatcher)

    vm.refresh()
    assertEquals(FeedUiState.Loading, vm.uiState.value)
    advanceTimeBy(1_000)
    runCurrent()
    assertEquals(FeedUiState.Content(items), vm.uiState.value)
}

callouts.title: Share the Scheduler
callouts.text: Every TestDispatcher in a test must use testScheduler. Independent schedulers create work that advanceUntilIdle cannot see and produce hanging or flaky tests.

subtopics.title: Replace Dispatchers.Main
subtopics.description: ViewModels use Main by default. Install a test dispatcher before construction and always reset it afterward through a rule/extension.

callouts.title: Standard vs Unconfined
callouts.text: StandardTestDispatcher queues work for precise control. UnconfinedTestDispatcher eagerly enters launched coroutines and can simplify collection, but it does not model production scheduling order.

subtopics.title: Finite Flow, StateFlow & Ongoing Collection
subtopics.description: Use first/take/toList for finite assertions. Activate stateIn WhileSubscribed streams with a background collector and cancel it automatically with backgroundScope.

tabs.label: Finite
tabs.code:
val values = repository.events.take(3).toList()
assertEquals(listOf(A, B, C), values)

callouts.title: Never Await an Infinite Flow
callouts.text: toList on an infinite stream never completes. Bound collection, use a background collector, or use a dedicated Flow assertion library with explicit cancellation.

sections.title: Instrumented & Integration Tests
sections.description: Run on a device when Android framework behavior, resources, storage, or real rendering matters.

subtopics.title: Choose the Correct Environment
subtopics.description: Local JVM tests are fastest; Robolectric can emulate selected framework behavior; instrumented tests provide real runtime and device integration.

codeBlocks.code:
Pure logic/contract → local JVM
Resource/configuration behavior with supported shadows → Robolectric
Room migration and SQLite behavior → device/emulator test
Permissions, intents, services, rendering → device/emulator
Critical OEM/API/form-factor behavior → representative device matrix

callouts.title: Use the Lowest Faithful Layer
callouts.text: Moving every test onto a device slows feedback. Keeping framework-dependent behavior out of business logic reduces both test cost and production coupling.

subtopics.title: Database & Migration Tests
subtopics.description: Test DAO behavior and every supported historical migration path against actual schemas.

callouts.title: Export Schemas
callouts.text: Migration tests require historical schema artifacts. Keep them in version control and test upgrade paths used by real installed versions.

sections.title: Compose UI, Semantics & Navigation
sections.description: Interact as a user through the semantics tree and assert visible outcomes.

subtopics.title: Compose Test Rule & Semantics
subtopics.description: Find nodes by accessible text, content description, role, state, or stable test tag only when user-facing semantics are insufficient.

callouts.title: Semantics Improve Accessibility Too
callouts.text: Tests that query meaningful roles, labels, and states encourage an accessible UI. Test tags are implementation hooks; use them sparingly for otherwise ambiguous nodes.

subtopics.title: Synchronization & Animation Clock
subtopics.description: Compose tests synchronize with known Compose work. Control the main clock for animations or delayed UI behavior.

callouts.title: External Work Needs Idling
callouts.text: Compose cannot automatically observe every executor, callback, or network client. Inject controllable dependencies or register an idling resource rather than sleeping.

subtopics.title: Navigation & Back Stack
subtopics.description: Test destinations through a test navigation controller or host and assert route/back-stack outcomes after user actions.

codeBlocks.code:
Test deep-link entry and invalid arguments
Test forward navigation after user action
Test Up versus system Back semantics
Test result delivery and cancelled flows
Test state restoration after recreation
Keep navigation callbacks injectable in isolated screen tests

callouts.title: Do Not Mock NavController Deeply
callouts.text: A real test navigation host gives more confidence in route configuration and back-stack behavior than verifying method calls on a mock.

sections.title: Reliability, Performance & CI
sections.description: Make failures reproducible and keep the suite fast enough to run continuously.

subtopics.title: Eliminate Flaky Tests
subtopics.description: Control time, randomness, locale, network, storage, dispatchers, and shared state. Wait for conditions, never arbitrary time.

codeBlocks.code:
Replace sleep with scheduler/idling/condition synchronization
Inject Clock and deterministic Random
Use hermetic fake server responses
Reset databases, files, preferences, and app state
Avoid test ordering and global mutable fixtures
Capture seed, API level, locale, and device configuration on failure
Treat retries as diagnosis telemetry, not a fix

callouts.title: Quarantine With Ownership
callouts.text: A flaky test erodes trust in all failures. If quarantine is unavoidable, assign an owner and expiry while preserving failure evidence.

subtopics.title: CI Layers & Device Matrix
subtopics.description: Run fast checks on every change, broader device suites after merge, and release-critical journeys before deployment.

codeBlocks.code:
Pull request: compile, lint, local unit tests, focused UI smoke
Main branch: integration, migrations, broader instrumented suite
Nightly: API/form-factor/locale matrix, accessibility, stress
Release: critical journeys, upgrade path, performance baselines
Track duration, flake rate, failure clusters, and slowest tests

callouts.title: Shard by Historical Duration
callouts.text: Balance shards using measured runtime rather than test count. Keep emulator snapshots and dependencies pinned so infrastructure changes are deliberate.

subtopics.title: Test Review Checklist
subtopics.description: Review value, determinism, isolation, readability, fidelity, and failure diagnostics.

codeBlocks.code:
□ Test name states behavior and condition
□ Assertions cover an observable contract
□ Correct environment is used
□ Time and dispatchers are controllable
□ No sleeps, live network, or order dependence
□ Fakes preserve important contract semantics
□ Cleanup runs even after assertion failure
□ Failure output identifies expected versus actual
□ Error, cancellation, empty, and restoration paths exist
□ UI queries use meaningful semantics
□ Migration paths and critical journeys are represented
□ Suite placement matches feedback-speed needs
